$comment: G7. Paths an automated branch may not touch: they define what the system may do and what it may read. An automation that can edit its own limits has none. This list is the single home; gate-protected-paths.sh checks that the fenced block under '## G7 — Protected paths' in docs/gate-requirements.md still says exactly the same thing, so the rule and its documentation cannot drift apart.
$comment_branch_prefixes: A branch prefix is a name the editor chooses, so it can only INCRIMINATE. Matching one is an admission and fails; not matching one proves nothing and is never an exculpation. Measured on PR #72: an agent raised MAX_TREE_BYTES inside scripts/gates/** on a branch it had itself named `loop/...`, and this gate passed it green. `loop/` was added on 2026-09-01: every improvement run of this repository works on a `loop/` branch, and without the prefix the only signal left there was the commit trailer - the one signal a harness can simply forget to write, which is how PR #72 went green. The cost of the hardening was measured before paying it: over the 12 most recent merged pull requests (#69-#80), 16 of 17 branch commits already carried the trailer, so the gate was already firing on those branches. The prefix adds no new red; it only stops the red from going out when nobody signs. Do not measure this on `main`: the squash rewrites the message with --body-file and drops the trailer, so `main` reads 10 of 40 and that is not the number this gate sees.

automation_commit_markers.$comment: Signals in the COMMIT RANGE rather than in the branch name. An agent does not type these; its harness writes them. They are still not proof of a human when absent - nothing available at gate time is - so they are read in one direction only, exactly like the prefix above.

content_exemptions.why: Measured 2026-09-01, from a user: 'hay un error en pr context gates'. G7 failed on EVERY Dependabot pull request in the github_actions ecosystem, and could never have passed one. `.github/workflows/**` became protected on 23c240f (2026-08-21); 9e17a07 (PR #73, 2026-09-01) added `dependabot`, `[bot]` and `github-actions` to identity_substrings. Each change was right on its own. Their intersection is unsatisfiable, because editing workflow files IS the work of that ecosystem. Proof it is a regression rather than a design: the same branch dependabot/github_actions/github-actions-0856f00088 went green on 2026-08-31 and red four times on 2026-09-01. PR #63 - a one-line bump of github/codeql-action/upload-sarif, a SECURITY action - has been red since 31 August.
content_exemptions.why_not_exempt_the_bot: Exempting Dependabot wholesale would open a real hole: a bot pull request that changes `permissions:`, adds a `run:` step or introduces a job is a supply-chain vector, and the bot identity is exactly what an attacker would forge. So the exemption is not about WHO edits, it is about WHAT changed. Every added and removed line in the file must be a `uses:` pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA. One line that is not - anywhere in that file - and the whole file stays protected.
content_exemptions.why_the_sha_is_required: A bump to a tag or a branch (`@v4`, `@main`) is a mutable reference and is NOT exempt: the whole reason this repository pins actions is that a tag can be moved under it. So the exemption can only ever make a pinned repo more pinned.
content_exemptions.fails_closed: The exemption needs the DIFF, not the file list. When the diff cannot be read the exemption does not apply and the file stays protected. A rule that turns into a pass when its input goes missing is the false green this repository has already been burned by once.

$comment_why_not_narrowed: MEASURED AND REFUSED, 2026-09-01. A task stood open to take the fixture INPUTS (`fixtures/*/bad/*`, `fixtures/*/unmeasurable/*`) out of `scripts/gates/**`, on the argument that they are negative proof rather than limits and that G7 fires on them for nothing. Both halves were measured against the 28 merged changes that tripped G7. Half one is true: 38 of the 150 paths it named were fixture inputs, 25%. Half two is FALSE: in 0 of those 28 changes did G7 fire on fixtures ALONE, so the exemption would have removed protection from 38 paths and prevented not one firing. And the three ways such a fixture can be weakened are watched by gates that answer a different question - the census asks whether it is still THERE, the family self-test asks whether it still TRIPS - while G7 is the only one that asks WHO moved it. `covered by another gate` is not `covered`. What the measurement did show is real and is fixed instead by `listing_fold` below: on the worst change 2 genuine limits were buried under 19 lines of fixture.

listing_fold.$comment: A DISPLAY decision and nothing else. These patterns are protected exactly as before: an automation touching one still FAILS, and a failing G7 names every path in full, as does a path moved under an override label. What folds is the UNATTRIBUTED listing - the one a maintainer reads to decide where to look - because a list where the two lines that matter sit under nineteen that do not is a list nobody reads to the end. Removing a control and burying it in noise are the same edit; this folds the noise and removes no control. Patterns here are plain fnmatch, where `*` crosses `/`; they are NOT the `/**` form used in `paths`.

groups.label: negative-proof inputs
groups.watched_by: deletion by gate-negative-proof-census.sh, which fails when the count on disk drops below the declared one; neutering in place by the family's own self-test, which names the rule the fixture stopped tripping and caps the verdict at 2
